_**Code 8**_ is a 2019 Canadian [superhero film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Superhero_film "Superhero film") written and directed by Jeff Chan, and starring the cousins [Stephen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell "Stephen Amell") and [Robbie Amell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robbie_Amell "Robbie Amell"). It is a feature-length version of the [2016 short film of the same name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Code_8_(2016_film) "Code 8 (2016 film)") about a man with superhuman abilities who works with a group of criminals to raise money to help his sick mother.

_Code 8_ was released [theatrically](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theatrical_release "Theatrical release") in December 2019, with [Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix") releasing it for [streaming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Streaming "Streaming") in April 2020.

The film's sequel, _[Code 8: Part II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Code\_8:\_Part\_II "Code 8: Part II")_, was released on [Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix") on February 28, 2024. Robbie and Stephen Amell, as well as [Aaron Abrams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Abrams "Aaron Abrams") and [Alex Mallari Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Mallari_Jr. "Alex Mallari Jr."), reprise their roles.

## Plot

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Code_8_(2019_film)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Plot")]

In the early 20th century, the public becomes aware of people with [superhuman abilities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Superhuman_abilities "Superhuman abilities"), known as Powers, resulting in the government passing a law requiring all Powers to register their abilities. Powers become key to the workforce, specifically noted as having helped build Lincoln City as "the city of tomorrow", creating an economic boom. However, as the [Third Industrial Revolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Third_Industrial_Revolution "Third Industrial Revolution") begins, Powers are marginalized in the face of increased automation and mechanization.

By the 1990s, a crime syndicate known as the Trust has flooded the streets with an addictive drug called Psyke, made from the spinal fluid of trafficked Powers. Police departments begin using drone-deployed robots, called Guardians, and facial recognition software to combat Power-related crime while a citywide Powers ban is debated.

Connor Reed, a 26-year-old Electric ([electrokinetic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elektrokinesis?action=edit&redlink=1 "Elektrokinesis (page does not exist)")) looks after his mother, Mary, a Cryo ([cryokinetic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cryokinetic?action=edit&redlink=1 "Cryokinetic (page does not exist)")), whose ailment impedes her from controlling her powers. Due to their status as Powers, finding decent work is difficult, leaving them unable to afford treatment for Mary's condition. Connor makes ends meet by working as an unregistered day laborer alongside other Powers. Elsewhere in the city, a drug raid is conducted by detectives Alex Park and Davis on an apartment complex owned by crime lord Marcus Sutcliffe, the local agent of the Trust and a Reader ([mind reader](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Telepathy "Telepathy")). Marcus is confronted by his superior Westley Cumbo and told to pay his cut to the Trust soon or face consequences.

Connor is approached by Garrett—Marcus' underling and a TK ([telekinetic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Telekinetic "Telekinetic"))—and his crew for a job, which turns out to be a robbery of a chemical plant. Connor shorts out an electrical fence in an impressive display of power, piquing Garrett's interest. He is introduced to Marcus and meets Nia, Marcus's apparent girlfriend. Park and Davis arrive at the robbery scene the next day and determine that the stolen chemicals are being used to cut Psyke, indicating Marcus is desperate for revenue.

Garrett recruits Connor for more jobs while training him to maximize his abilities and agrees to help him earn enough money to get Mary's treatment. Connor grows close with Garrett's crew—Freddie, a mute Brawn (super strength), and Maddy, a Pyro ([pyrokinetic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pyrokinetic "Pyrokinetic")).

Marcus has the crew rob a bank to pay back the Trust, but the vault contains only a tenth of the money they expected. Wesley's Shifter (shapeshifter) assassin, Copperhead, attempts to kill Marcus for not honoring his debt, but Marcus's bodyguard Rhino, a Brawn with bulletproof skin, kills them. Nia reveals to Connor that she is a Healer, and only remains with Marcus to ease the effects of his Psyke addiction and pay off her imprisoned father's debt.

Mary's condition worsens, and the doctors tell Connor that they need to operate soon to save her. Park and Davis bring Connor in for questioning. Davis wants to plant evidence and coerce him into informing. Park cuts him loose due to lack of evidence. He is revealed to have a daughter who is a TK, and who fears she will be given up because of her difficulty with controlling her powers.

When Connor is released he goes to Garrett and suggests they rob a police-confiscated Psyke transport, which will make them $10 million. They bring the idea to Marcus, where Connor demands Nia heal Mary as payment, while Garrett wants to be made equal partners with Marcus.

On the day of the heist, the crew blocks the transport inside a [no-fly zone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/No-fly_zone "No-fly zone"), preventing backup by drones carrying Guardians. Although they manage to retrieve the Psyke non-lethally, Marcus's men execute police officers and betray them. They kill Maddy and fatally wound Freddie, while Rhino flees with the drugs. Connor tells Garrett that Marcus framed them because of Garrett's demands, and they part ways.

Connor contacts Park and offers up Marcus's hideout. The cops raid it while Connor and Garrett team up to fight and kill both Rhino and Marcus. Garrett takes the Psyke and encourages Connor to use Nia to heal his mother. She pleads with Connor to let her go, as her abilities force her to take the injury or disease onto herself. He takes Nia to the hospital at gunpoint to cure his mother, but changes his mind after having a flashback. Mary dies soon after.

Connor gives Nia his truck to leave the city, while Garrett hands over the Psyke to Wesley and takes over the drug trade for the Trust in Lincoln City. Connor visits his mother's grave before he surrenders himself to the police, while Nia has a tearful visit with her father. Meanwhile, the Powers Ban is being voted on while Park reluctantly accepts an award for the successful raid.

## Production

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Code_8_(2019_film)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Production")]

In 2016, Robbie and Stephen Amell released a short film, _[Code 8](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Code\_8\_(2016\_film) "Code 8 (2016 film)")_, which acted as a teaser for a potential feature film. An [Indiegogo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indiegogo "Indiegogo") fundraising campaign asking for $200,000 was launched on March 23 and reached $2.4 million by April 24.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Code_8_(2019_film)#cite_note-Indiegogo-3) Fundraising closed with $3.4 million on December 31, 2019, with the continued campaign helping recover costs of DVD pressings and the distribution to contributors of perks, wardrobe, and props from the production.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Code_8_(2019_film)#cite_note-Indiegogo-3) A four-minute segment of the film's closing credits shows a list of only some of the 30,810 contributors[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Code_8_(2019_film)#cite_note-Indiegogo-3) to the fundraising campaign.

The first announcement of additional cast came on June 12, 2017, when Laysla De Oliveira joined.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Code_8_(2019_film)#cite_note-4)

[Principal photography](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Principal_photography "Principal photography") began on June 1, 2017, in [Toronto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toronto "Toronto").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Code_8_(2019_film)#cite_note-5)

Ryan Taubert composed the film score, and [Sony Masterworks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Masterworks "Sony Masterworks") released the soundtrack.

## Release

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Code_8_(2019_film)&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Release")]

On February 9, 2017, during the [Berlin International Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin_International_Film_Festival "Berlin International Film Festival"), [XYZ Films](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/XYZ_Films "XYZ Films") acquired the international sales rights for the film.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Code_8_(2019_film)#cite_note-6)

The film was released theatrically in Canada on December 6, 2019 and in the United States on December 13, 2019; its streaming release on [Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix") followed on April 11, 2020.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Code_8_(2019_film)#cite_note-7)

## Reception

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Code_8_(2019_film)&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Reception")]

On the [review aggregator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Review_aggregator "Review aggregator") website [Rotten Tomatoes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotten_Tomatoes "Rotten Tomatoes"), 85% of 20 critics' reviews are positive, with an average rating of 6.4/10.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Code_8_(2019_film)#cite_note-Rotten_Tomatoes-8)[Metacritic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metacritic "Metacritic"), which uses a [weighted average](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weighted_arithmetic_mean "Weighted arithmetic mean"), assigned the film a score of 48 out of 100, based on five critics, indicating "mixed or average" reviews.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Code_8_(2019_film)#cite_note-Metacritic-9)

Dennis Harvey of _[Variety](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Variety\_(magazine) "Variety (magazine)")_ found the crowdfunded _Code 8_ a "solid genre effort" that "is resourceful and polished on a tight budget". He noted a few limitations, for example a screenplay that "packs in a lot of characters and complications without much time to lend them distinguishing personality", not enough humor to transcend the "sentimental cliché" of a mother needing medical treatment, and a "lack of stylistically bold elements in the competent action sequences". He nevertheless thought the film a "well-crafted mix of crime melodrama and fantasy" with "generally strong" performances from its actors, and visual effects that "present a plausible near-future", and that this feature represented an "impressive leap in scale" from Chan's 2014 debut film.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Code_8_(2019_film)#cite_note-10)

Noel Murray of _[Los Angeles Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los\_Angeles\_Times "Los Angeles Times")_ wrote that while the movie had "clearly been made with passion and intelligence", the "ideas outpace the action" and it was made "without the kind of zip that this kind of story demands".[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Code_8_(2019_film)#cite_note-11)

In April 2020, the film appeared on the Top 10 Netflix list for the United States.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Code_8_(2019_film)#cite_note-Wired-12)

## Future

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Code_8_(2019_film)&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Future")]

### Spin-off series

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Code_8_(2019_film)&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Spin-off series")]

In December 2019, a short-form spin-off series was announced to be in development at [Quibi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quibi "Quibi"), starring Robbie and Stephen Amell, written by Chris Pare, and directed by Jeff Chan.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Code_8_(2019_film)#cite_note-13) Following the announcement that Quibi was shutting down, the series was left in limbo.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Code_8_(2019_film)#cite_note-14)

### Sequel

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Code_8_(2019_film)&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Sequel")]

Main article: [Code 8: Part II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Code_8:_Part_II "Code 8: Part II")

In June 2021, Robbie and Stephen Amell reprised their roles in the [sequel film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Code_8:_Part_II "Code 8: Part II") that was released in 2024.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Code_8_(2019_film)#cite_note-15)[Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix") acquired the global rights to the film.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Code_8_(2019_film)#cite_note-16)

_**Code 8**_ is a 2019 Canadian [superhero film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Superhero_film "Superhero film") written and directed by Jeff Chan, and starring the cousins [Stephen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell "Stephen Amell") and [Robbie Amell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robbie_Amell "Robbie Amell"). It is a feature-length version of the [2016 short film of the same name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Code_8_(2016_film) "Code 8 (2016 film)") about a man with superhuman abilities who works with a group of criminals to raise money to help his sick mother.

_Code 8_ was released [theatrically](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theatrical_release "Theatrical release") in December 2019, with [Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix") releasing it for [streaming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Streaming "Streaming") in April 2020.

The film's sequel, _[Code 8: Part II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Code\_8:\_Part\_II "Code 8: Part II")_, was released on [Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix") on February 28, 2024. Robbie and Stephen Amell, as well as [Aaron Abrams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Abrams "Aaron Abrams") and [Alex Mallari Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Mallari_Jr. "Alex Mallari Jr."), reprise their roles.

## Plot

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Code_8_(2019_film)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Plot")]

In the early 20th century, the public becomes aware of people with [superhuman abilities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Superhuman_abilities "Superhuman abilities"), known as Powers, resulting in the government passing a law requiring all Powers to register their abilities. Powers become key to the workforce, specifically noted as having helped build Lincoln City as "the city of tomorrow", creating an economic boom. However, as the [Third Industrial Revolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Third_Industrial_Revolution "Third Industrial Revolution") begins, Powers are marginalized in the face of increased automation and mechanization.

By the 1990s, a crime syndicate known as the Trust has flooded the streets with an addictive drug called Psyke, made from the spinal fluid of trafficked Powers. Police departments begin using drone-deployed robots, called Guardians, and facial recognition software to combat Power-related crime while a citywide Powers ban is debated.

Connor Reed, a 26-year-old Electric ([electrokinetic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elektrokinesis?action=edit&redlink=1 "Elektrokinesis (page does not exist)")) looks after his mother, Mary, a Cryo ([cryokinetic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cryokinetic?action=edit&redlink=1 "Cryokinetic (page does not exist)")), whose ailment impedes her from controlling her powers. Due to their status as Powers, finding decent work is difficult, leaving them unable to afford treatment for Mary's condition. Connor makes ends meet by working as an unregistered day laborer alongside other Powers. Elsewhere in the city, a drug raid is conducted by detectives Alex Park and Davis on an apartment complex owned by crime lord Marcus Sutcliffe, the local agent of the Trust and a Reader ([mind reader](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Telepathy "Telepathy")). Marcus is confronted by his superior Westley Cumbo and told to pay his cut to the Trust soon or face consequences.

Connor is approached by Garrett—Marcus' underling and a TK ([telekinetic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Telekinetic "Telekinetic"))—and his crew for a job, which turns out to be a robbery of a chemical plant. Connor shorts out an electrical fence in an impressive display of power, piquing Garrett's interest. He is introduced to Marcus and meets Nia, Marcus's apparent girlfriend. Park and Davis arrive at the robbery scene the next day and determine that the stolen chemicals are being used to cut Psyke, indicating Marcus is desperate for revenue.

Garrett recruits Connor for more jobs while training him to maximize his abilities and agrees to help him earn enough money to get Mary's treatment. Connor grows close with Garrett's crew—Freddie, a mute Brawn (super strength), and Maddy, a Pyro ([pyrokinetic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pyrokinetic "Pyrokinetic")).

Marcus has the crew rob a bank to pay back the Trust, but the vault contains only a tenth of the money they expected. Wesley's Shifter (shapeshifter) assassin, Copperhead, attempts to kill Marcus for not honoring his debt, but Marcus's bodyguard Rhino, a Brawn with bulletproof skin, kills them. Nia reveals to Connor that she is a Healer, and only remains with Marcus to ease the effects of his Psyke addiction and pay off her imprisoned father's debt.

Mary's condition worsens, and the doctors tell Connor that they need to operate soon to save her. Park and Davis bring Connor in for questioning. Davis wants to plant evidence and coerce him into informing. Park cuts him loose due to lack of evidence. He is revealed to have a daughter who is a TK, and who fears she will be given up because of her difficulty with controlling her powers.

When Connor is released he goes to Garrett and suggests they rob a police-confiscated Psyke transport, which will make them $10 million. They bring the idea to Marcus, where Connor demands Nia heal Mary as payment, while Garrett wants to be made equal partners with Marcus.

On the day of the heist, the crew blocks the transport inside a [no-fly zone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/No-fly_zone "No-fly zone"), preventing backup by drones carrying Guardians. Although they manage to retrieve the Psyke non-lethally, Marcus's men execute police officers and betray them. They kill Maddy and fatally wound Freddie, while Rhino flees with the drugs. Connor tells Garrett that Marcus framed them because of Garrett's demands, and they part ways.

Connor contacts Park and offers up Marcus's hideout. The cops raid it while Connor and Garrett team up to fight and kill both Rhino and Marcus. Garrett takes the Psyke and encourages Connor to use Nia to heal his mother. She pleads with Connor to let her go, as her abilities force her to take the injury or disease onto herself. He takes Nia to the hospital at gunpoint to cure his mother, but changes his mind after having a flashback. Mary dies soon after.

Connor gives Nia his truck to leave the city, while Garrett hands over the Psyke to Wesley and takes over the drug trade for the Trust in Lincoln City. Connor visits his mother's grave before he surrenders himself to the police, while Nia has a tearful visit with her father. Meanwhile, the Powers Ban is being voted on while Park reluctantly accepts an award for the successful raid.

## Production

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Code_8_(2019_film)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Production")]

In 2016, Robbie and Stephen Amell released a short film, _[Code 8](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Code\_8\_(2016\_film) "Code 8 (2016 film)")_, which acted as a teaser for a potential feature film. An [Indiegogo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indiegogo "Indiegogo") fundraising campaign asking for $200,000 was launched on March 23 and reached $2.4 million by April 24.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Code_8_(2019_film)#cite_note-Indiegogo-3) Fundraising closed with $3.4 million on December 31, 2019, with the continued campaign helping recover costs of DVD pressings and the distribution to contributors of perks, wardrobe, and props from the production.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Code_8_(2019_film)#cite_note-Indiegogo-3) A four-minute segment of the film's closing credits shows a list of only some of the 30,810 contributors[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Code_8_(2019_film)#cite_note-Indiegogo-3) to the fundraising campaign.

The first announcement of additional cast came on June 12, 2017, when Laysla De Oliveira joined.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Code_8_(2019_film)#cite_note-4)

[Principal photography](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Principal_photography "Principal photography") began on June 1, 2017, in [Toronto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toronto "Toronto").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Code_8_(2019_film)#cite_note-5)

Ryan Taubert composed the film score, and [Sony Masterworks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Masterworks "Sony Masterworks") released the soundtrack.

## Release

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Code_8_(2019_film)&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Release")]

On February 9, 2017, during the [Berlin International Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin_International_Film_Festival "Berlin International Film Festival"), [XYZ Films](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/XYZ_Films "XYZ Films") acquired the international sales rights for the film.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Code_8_(2019_film)#cite_note-6)

The film was released theatrically in Canada on December 6, 2019 and in the United States on December 13, 2019; its streaming release on [Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix") followed on April 11, 2020.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Code_8_(2019_film)#cite_note-7)

## Reception

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Code_8_(2019_film)&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Reception")]

On the [review aggregator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Review_aggregator "Review aggregator") website [Rotten Tomatoes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotten_Tomatoes "Rotten Tomatoes"), 85% of 20 critics' reviews are positive, with an average rating of 6.4/10.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Code_8_(2019_film)#cite_note-Rotten_Tomatoes-8)[Metacritic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metacritic "Metacritic"), which uses a [weighted average](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weighted_arithmetic_mean "Weighted arithmetic mean"), assigned the film a score of 48 out of 100, based on five critics, indicating "mixed or average" reviews.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Code_8_(2019_film)#cite_note-Metacritic-9)

Dennis Harvey of _[Variety](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Variety\_(magazine) "Variety (magazine)")_ found the crowdfunded _Code 8_ a "solid genre effort" that "is resourceful and polished on a tight budget". He noted a few limitations, for example a screenplay that "packs in a lot of characters and complications without much time to lend them distinguishing personality", not enough humor to transcend the "sentimental cliché" of a mother needing medical treatment, and a "lack of stylistically bold elements in the competent action sequences". He nevertheless thought the film a "well-crafted mix of crime melodrama and fantasy" with "generally strong" performances from its actors, and visual effects that "present a plausible near-future", and that this feature represented an "impressive leap in scale" from Chan's 2014 debut film.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Code_8_(2019_film)#cite_note-10)

Noel Murray of _[Los Angeles Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los\_Angeles\_Times "Los Angeles Times")_ wrote that while the movie had "clearly been made with passion and intelligence", the "ideas outpace the action" and it was made "without the kind of zip that this kind of story demands".[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Code_8_(2019_film)#cite_note-11)

In April 2020, the film appeared on the Top 10 Netflix list for the United States.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Code_8_(2019_film)#cite_note-Wired-12)

## Future

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Code_8_(2019_film)&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Future")]

### Spin-off series

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Code_8_(2019_film)&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Spin-off series")]

In December 2019, a short-form spin-off series was announced to be in development at [Quibi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quibi "Quibi"), starring Robbie and Stephen Amell, written by Chris Pare, and directed by Jeff Chan.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Code_8_(2019_film)#cite_note-13) Following the announcement that Quibi was shutting down, the series was left in limbo.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Code_8_(2019_film)#cite_note-14)

### Sequel

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Code_8_(2019_film)&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Sequel")]

Main article: [Code 8: Part II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Code_8:_Part_II "Code 8: Part II")

In June 2021, Robbie and Stephen Amell reprised their roles in the [sequel film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Code_8:_Part_II "Code 8: Part II") that was released in 2024.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Code_8_(2019_film)#cite_note-15)[Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix") acquired the global rights to the film.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Code_8_(2019_film)#cite_note-16)

**Stephen Adam Amell**[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-1) (born May 8, 1981) is a Canadian-American actor. He came to prominence for playing the lead role of [Oliver Queen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oliver_Queen_(Arrowverse) "Oliver Queen (Arrowverse)") on [the CW](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_CW "The CW") superhero series _[Arrow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrow\_(TV\_series) "Arrow (TV series)")_ (2012–2020), based on [DC Comics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DC_Comics "DC Comics"). Amell also appeared in subsequent [Arrowverse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrowverse "Arrowverse") franchise media, along with reprising his role in various video games. Following the conclusion of _Arrow_, Amell landed the lead roles in both the [Starz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Starz "Starz") drama series _[Heels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heels\_(TV\_series) "Heels (TV series)")_ (2021–2023), and _[Suits LA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suits\_LA "Suits LA")_ (2025).

Outside of television, Amell portrayed [Casey Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Casey_Jones_(Teenage_Mutant_Ninja_Turtles) "Casey Jones (Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles)") in the superhero film _[Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Out of the Shadows](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teenage\_Mutant\_Ninja\_Turtles:\_Out\_of\_the\_Shadows "Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Out of the Shadows")_ (2016). Amell co-produced and starred in _[Code 8](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Code\_8\_(2019\_film) "Code 8 (2019 film)")_ and its sequel _[Code 8: Part II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Code\_8:\_Part\_II "Code 8: Part II")_ with his cousin [Robbie Amell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robbie_Amell "Robbie Amell"). He has also made a number of appearances in the [professional wrestling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Professional_wrestling "Professional wrestling") circuit.

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Stephen_Amell&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Stephen Adam Amell was born on May 8, 1981,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-2) in [Toronto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toronto "Toronto"), Ontario, the son of Sandra Anne (née Bolté) and Thomas J. Amell.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-4) He is a first cousin of actor [Robbie Amell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robbie_Amell "Robbie Amell").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-5) He attended [St. Andrew's College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Andrew's_College,_Aurora "St. Andrew's College, Aurora"), a private independent school for boys, and graduated in 2000.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-6)

## Acting career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Stephen_Amell&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Acting career")]

### 2004–2012: Early career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Stephen_Amell&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: 2004–2012: Early career")]

Amell appeared in two episodes of the [fourth season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queer_as_Folk_(season_4) "Queer as Folk (season 4)") of _[Queer as Folk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queer\_as\_Folk\_(2000\_TV\_series) "Queer as Folk (2000 TV series)")_ as the Liberty Ride spinning instructor in 2004. Amell played Adam in the first season of the television series _[Dante's Cove](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dante's\_Cove "Dante's Cove")_; he was replaced in the second season by Jon Fleming. In 2007, Amell won a [Gemini Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gemini_Awards "Gemini Awards") for his guest-starring role on _[ReGenesis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ReGenesis "ReGenesis")_.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-Free-7) The same year he was also nominated for a Gemini Award in the Best Ensemble Cast Category for _[Rent-a-Goalie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rent-a-Goalie "Rent-a-Goalie")_.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-8) He had recurring roles in the TV series _[Da Kink in My Hair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Da\_Kink\_in\_My\_Hair\_(TV\_series) "Da Kink in My Hair (TV series)")_ and _[Heartland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartland\_(Canadian\_TV\_series) "Heartland (Canadian TV series)")_. On December 3, 2010, Amell joined the cast of _[The Vampire Diaries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Vampire\_Diaries "The Vampire Diaries")_ as werewolf 'Brady' for season 2.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-9) Amell starred as the real life convicted killer [Joran van der Sloot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joran_van_der_Sloot "Joran van der Sloot") in the [Lifetime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lifetime_(TV_network) "Lifetime (TV network)") film _[Justice for Natalee Holloway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justice\_for\_Natalee\_Holloway "Justice for Natalee Holloway")_ which originally aired in May 2011.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-AV-10)

On October 2, 2011, season 3 of [HBO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HBO "HBO")'s series _[Hung](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hung\_(TV\_series) "Hung (TV series)")_ premiered with Amell starring as busboy-turned-prostitute Jason, a younger rival "ho" to [Thomas Jane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_Jane "Thomas Jane")'s Ray Drecker.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-Free-7) He also appeared as Jim in the [fourth season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/90210_(season_4) "90210 (season 4)") of _[90210](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/90210\_(TV\_series) "90210 (TV series)")_.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-TV-11) Amell announced on October 28, 2011, that he had just finished filming the Christmas episode of _[New Girl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New\_Girl "New Girl")_ with [Zooey Deschanel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zooey_Deschanel "Zooey Deschanel") and [Max Greenfield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Greenfield "Max Greenfield"). He touches on the experience of filming his first "network half-hour comedy" in an interview with _Daemon's TV_.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-TV-11) On November 9, 2011, Amell was announced for the recurring role of Scottie, a paramedic on [ABC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Broadcasting_Company "American Broadcasting Company")'s _[Private Practice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Private\_Practice\_(TV\_series) "Private Practice (TV series)")_.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-12) He also played the role of Travis McKenna in _[Blue Mountain State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blue\_Mountain\_State "Blue Mountain State")_.

### 2012–2020: _Arrow_

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Stephen_Amell&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: 2012–2020: Arrow")]

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4b/Stephen_Amell_2014.jpg/250px-Stephen_Amell_2014.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Stephen_Amell_2014.jpg)

Amell on the set of _[Arrow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrow\_(TV\_series) "Arrow (TV series)")_ in September 2014

In January 2012, Amell was cast as [Oliver Queen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oliver_Queen_(Arrowverse) "Oliver Queen (Arrowverse)") in [The CW](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_CW "The CW") series _[Arrow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrow\_(TV\_series) "Arrow (TV series)")_, based on the [DC Comics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DC_Comics "DC Comics") superhero [of the same name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_Arrow "Green Arrow").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-AV-10) This series and role led to Amell appearing as the character on other superhero series on the network as part of the growing [Arrowverse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrowverse "Arrowverse"), including _[The Flash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Flash\_(2014\_TV\_series) "The Flash (2014 TV series)")_, _[Legends of Tomorrow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legends\_of\_Tomorrow "Legends of Tomorrow")_, _[Supergirl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supergirl\_(TV\_series) "Supergirl (TV series)")_, and _[Batwoman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Batwoman\_(TV\_series) "Batwoman (TV series)")_, as well as the [CW Seed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CW_Seed "CW Seed") webseries _[Vixen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vixen\_(web\_series) "Vixen (web series)")_.

Amell co-starred in _[Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Out of the Shadows](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teenage\_Mutant\_Ninja\_Turtles:\_Out\_of\_the\_Shadows\_(film) "Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Out of the Shadows (film)")_ (released on June 3, 2016) as vigilante "[Casey Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Casey_Jones_(Teenage_Mutant_Ninja_Turtles) "Casey Jones (Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles)")".[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-13) Amell announced in May 2017 that he would be participating on a special celebrity edition of _[American Ninja Warrior](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American\_Ninja\_Warrior "American Ninja Warrior")_.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-14) Amell demonstrated great physical abilities which was reflective of his athleticism in his portrayal of Oliver Queen.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-15) In 2017, he took part in the directorial debut of former _[Heartland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartland\_(Canadian\_TV\_series) "Heartland (Canadian TV series)")_ co-star [Michelle Morgan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michelle_Morgan_(actress) "Michelle Morgan (actress)"), a short film entitled _Mi Madre, My Father_, playing the estranged father of a six-year-old girl. Morgan raised funds for the production through a crowdfunding campaign.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-Morgan-16) The film premiered at the 2018 [Cannes Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cannes_Film_Festival "Cannes Film Festival").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-Cannes-17)

In March 2019, Amell announced the end of _Arrow_ with its [eighth and final season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrow_season_8 "Arrow season 8"), which premiered in October 2019 and concluded in January 2020.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-18)

### 2020–present: Post-_Arrow_

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Stephen_Amell&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: 2020–present: Post-Arrow")]

His first post-_Arrow_ project was announced in August 2019 as _[Heels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heels\_(TV\_series) "Heels (TV series)")_, a [Starz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Starz "Starz") drama series set in the world of [independent professional wrestling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Independent_professional_wrestling "Independent professional wrestling").[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-19) In December of the same year, it was announced that short-form streaming platform [Quibi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quibi "Quibi") were developing a spin-off series starring Amell and his cousin Robbie Amell, developed from their crowd-funded film _[Code 8](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Code\_8\_(2019\_film) "Code 8 (2019 film)")_.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-20) In September 2023, _Heels_ was canceled after two seasons.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-21) In February 2024, Stephen Amell was cast as Ted Black in the upcoming [NBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBC "NBC") pilot _Suits LA_, based on the [USA Network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USA_Network "USA Network") original series _[Suits](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suits\_(American\_TV\_series) "Suits (American TV series)")_.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-22) On July 19, 2024, _[Suits LA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suits\_LA "Suits LA")_ has ordered to series by NBC.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-23)

Amell plays Henry Roland, a police officer, in the [Crave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crave_(TV_network) "Crave (TV network)") crime drama series _[The Borderline](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Borderline\_(Canadian\_TV\_series) "The Borderline (Canadian TV series)")_.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-24) it debuted in February 2026.

He garnered positive reviews for his leading role in the Canadian crime film _[Little Lorraine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Little\_Lorraine "Little Lorraine")_, released in 2026.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-25)

## Professional wrestling career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Stephen_Amell&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Professional wrestling career")]

### WWE (2015)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Stephen_Amell&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: WWE (2015)")]

As an avid [professional wrestling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Professional_wrestling "Professional wrestling") fan,[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-HollywoodLifeWWE-26) Amell campaigned for a guest appearance on [WWE](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WWE "WWE")'s weekly _[Raw](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WWE\_Raw "WWE Raw")_ program.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-27)

In May 2015, it was reported that he was set to wrestle [Stardust (Cody Rhodes)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cody_Rhodes "Cody Rhodes") at WWE's [SummerSlam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SummerSlam_(2015) "SummerSlam (2015)") pay-per-view in August.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-HollywoodLifeWWE-26) Amell made his first WWE appearance on the May 25 episode of _Raw_, where he had a confrontation with Stardust.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-28) Amell returned to _Raw_ in early August; after being assaulted in the audience by Stardust, Amell got into the [ring](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wrestling_ring "Wrestling ring") to attack him until being contained by security. Following a [backstage segment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glossary_of_professional_wrestling_terms#Segment "Glossary of professional wrestling terms") with [Triple H](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Triple_H "Triple H"), it was announced that [Neville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neville_(wrestler) "Neville (wrestler)") would team with Amell to face Stardust and [King Barrett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wade_Barrett "Wade Barrett") at SummerSlam.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-29)

At the event on August 23, 2015, Amell and Neville defeated Barrett and Stardust in a [tag team match](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Professional_wrestling_tag_team_match_types "Professional wrestling tag team match types"). Amell participated in the wrestling, and, behind the scenes, wrestlers were said to have been impressed with Amell's performance.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-30)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-31) Amell became friends with Rhodes, with whom he later also worked on _Arrow_.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-BulletClub-32)

On December 21, 2015, Amell was awarded a [Slammy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slammy "Slammy") for the "Celebrity Moment of the Year" for his dive onto Stardust during the match.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-33)

### Ring of Honor (2017)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Stephen_Amell&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Ring of Honor (2017)")]

Amell returned to professional wrestling for [Ring of Honor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ring_of_Honor "Ring of Honor") on November 17, 2017, at [Survival of the Fittest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Survival_of_the_Fittest_(2017) "Survival of the Fittest (2017)").[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-34) On the day of the show, Amell joined the [Bullet Club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bullet_Club "Bullet Club")[faction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glossary_of_professional_wrestling_terms#Stable "Glossary of professional wrestling terms"), and teamed with Cody Rhodes, [Kenny Omega](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Omega "Kenny Omega"), and [The Young Bucks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Young_Bucks "The Young Bucks") (Matt and Nick Jackson) in a five-on-four tag team match. They defeated [The Addiction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Addiction_(professional_wrestling) "The Addiction (professional wrestling)") ([Christopher Daniels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Daniels "Christopher Daniels") and [Frankie Kazarian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frankie_Kazarian "Frankie Kazarian")), [Flip Gordon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flip_Gordon "Flip Gordon"), and [Scorpio Sky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scorpio_Sky "Scorpio Sky"), and Amell again participated in the wrestling, including being put through a table by The Addiction.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-35)

### All In (2018)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Stephen_Amell&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: All In (2018)")]

On August 6, 2018, it was announced that Amell would be competing at [All In](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_In_(professional_wrestling_event) "All In (professional wrestling event)"), in his first-ever singles match, where he was defeated by Christopher Daniels.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-36)

### All Elite Wrestling (2020)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Stephen_Amell&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: All Elite Wrestling (2020)")]

On February 29, 2020, Amell made an appearance at [All Elite Wrestling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Elite_Wrestling "All Elite Wrestling")'s [Revolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Revolution_(2020) "Revolution (2020)"), where he accompanied [Cody Rhodes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cody_Rhodes "Cody Rhodes") alongside Rhodes' [Nightmare Family](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nightmare_Family "Nightmare Family") for his match against [MJF](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maxwell_Jacob_Friedman "Maxwell Jacob Friedman").[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-37)

## Philanthropy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Stephen_Amell&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Philanthropy")]

Amell has hosted a number of successful fundraising campaigns via the crowd funded merchandise platform [Represent.com](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Represent.com "Represent.com").[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-38) In 2014, Amell partnered with the charity Fuck Cancer to raise almost a million dollars with the release of a T-shirt featuring his face on the front (with a Post-it note on his forehead and featuring the organization's name). He ended up selling over 60,000 shirts from this campaign.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-39) In January 2015, Amell launched his second Represent.com campaign featuring a word he made up, _Sinceriously_, to benefit two mental health charities: Paws and Stripes and Stand For The Silent.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] In August 2015, Amell used his guest appearance on _[WWE Raw](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WWE\_Raw "WWE Raw")_ with [Stardust](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cody_Rhodes "Cody Rhodes") to raise funds via his third campaign for children's hospice Emily's House in Toronto. The campaign raised $300,000, and Amell and Stardust presented a cheque together at Emily's House.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-40) During the Red Nose Day special of _[American Ninja Warrior](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American\_Ninja\_Warrior "American Ninja Warrior")_, Amell donated $35,000 for completing all six obstacles, and an extra obstacle, the Salmon Ladder.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-41)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Stephen_Amell&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Amell married his first wife, fellow Canadian Carolyn Lawrence, on December 8, 2007, in Toronto.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-42) The couple divorced in 2010.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-43) Amell married actress and model [Cassandra Jean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cassandra_Jean "Cassandra Jean") on December 25, 2012, in a private ceremony in [the Caribbean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Caribbean "The Caribbean"),[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-44) and for a second time in [New Orleans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Orleans "New Orleans") on May 26, 2013.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-45) The couple have a daughter who was born on October 15, 2013. They have a son, born May 13, 2022.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-46) Amell revealed on his Instagram that he became a dual citizen of Canada and the United States and took his U.S. citizenship oath in August 2022 at Dodger Stadium.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-47)

## Controversies

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Stephen_Amell&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Controversies")]

Amell's statements and behavior have occasionally drawn controversy. In September 2015, after a [Muslim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muslims "Muslims") student was arrested for [bringing a disassembled digital clock to his high school](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmed_Mohamed_clock_incident "Ahmed Mohamed clock incident") in [Irving](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irving,_Texas "Irving, Texas"), Texas, Amell tweeted, "Stereotyping Texas isn't any better than stereotyping Ahmed".[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-48) The post drew criticism online, prompting Amell to take a break from social media.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-49)[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-50)[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-51)

In 2018, Amell tweeted "my âpölògīés"[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-52) in response to criticism about his failure to use the [acute accent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acute_accent "Acute accent") while tweeting singer [Beyoncé](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beyonc%C3%A9 "Beyoncé")'s name.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-53)[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-54) After he was accused by online commenters of disrespecting [black names](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African-American_names "African-American names"), he said he had omitted the accent while being "lazy in the midst of a mediocre joke".[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-55)

In 2020, during the [Black Lives Matter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Lives_Matter "Black Lives Matter")[protests](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Floyd_protests "George Floyd protests"), Amell was criticized by comic book writer [Tee Franklin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tee_Franklin "Tee Franklin") and others for saying that racism is a systemic problem but that he had not personally "seen it in action".[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-56)

In 2021, Amell was asked to leave a [Delta Air Lines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delta_Air_Lines "Delta Air Lines") flight traveling from Austin to Los Angeles for yelling at his wife.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-57) He later said he was intoxicated at the time.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-58)[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-59)

In July 2023, Amell was criticized for comments he made at a fan convention regarding the [2023 SAG-AFTRA strike](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_SAG-AFTRA_strike "2023 SAG-AFTRA strike"). While he expressed support for [SAG-AFTRA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SAG-AFTRA "SAG-AFTRA") as his union, he called striking a "reductive negotiating tactic" and "myopic" and seemed to criticize that the strike banned him from promoting the second season of _Heels_.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-60)[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-61) He later clarified his opinion, saying that while he does not like striking, he "[understands] fundamentally why we're here" and stated that his support for the union was unconditional and that he stood with them.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-62) Amell did not attend the _Arrow_ cast reunion on the picket line outside the Warner Bros. studio lot in [Burbank, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burbank,_California "Burbank, California"), as he was in New York City at the time, but on the day of the reunion, he was photographed on the picket line in front of the [Warner Bros. Discovery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warner_Bros._Discovery "Warner Bros. Discovery") offices in New York and reportedly sent his regards to his former showrunners in California. [Marc Guggenheim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marc_Guggenheim "Marc Guggenheim"), executive producer of _Arrow_ and organizer of the revival, interpreted his attendance in New York as a symbolic stand in solidarity.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-63)[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-64)

**Stephen Adam Amell**[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-1) (born May 8, 1981) is a Canadian-American actor. He came to prominence for playing the lead role of [Oliver Queen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oliver_Queen_(Arrowverse) "Oliver Queen (Arrowverse)") on [the CW](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_CW "The CW") superhero series _[Arrow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrow\_(TV\_series) "Arrow (TV series)")_ (2012–2020), based on [DC Comics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DC_Comics "DC Comics"). Amell also appeared in subsequent [Arrowverse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrowverse "Arrowverse") franchise media, along with reprising his role in various video games. Following the conclusion of _Arrow_, Amell landed the lead roles in both the [Starz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Starz "Starz") drama series _[Heels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heels\_(TV\_series) "Heels (TV series)")_ (2021–2023), and _[Suits LA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suits\_LA "Suits LA")_ (2025).

Outside of television, Amell portrayed [Casey Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Casey_Jones_(Teenage_Mutant_Ninja_Turtles) "Casey Jones (Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles)") in the superhero film _[Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Out of the Shadows](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teenage\_Mutant\_Ninja\_Turtles:\_Out\_of\_the\_Shadows "Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Out of the Shadows")_ (2016). Amell co-produced and starred in _[Code 8](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Code\_8\_(2019\_film) "Code 8 (2019 film)")_ and its sequel _[Code 8: Part II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Code\_8:\_Part\_II "Code 8: Part II")_ with his cousin [Robbie Amell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robbie_Amell "Robbie Amell"). He has also made a number of appearances in the [professional wrestling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Professional_wrestling "Professional wrestling") circuit.

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Stephen_Amell&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Stephen Adam Amell was born on May 8, 1981,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-2) in [Toronto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toronto "Toronto"), Ontario, the son of Sandra Anne (née Bolté) and Thomas J. Amell.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-4) He is a first cousin of actor [Robbie Amell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robbie_Amell "Robbie Amell").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-5) He attended [St. Andrew's College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Andrew's_College,_Aurora "St. Andrew's College, Aurora"), a private independent school for boys, and graduated in 2000.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-6)

## Acting career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Stephen_Amell&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Acting career")]

### 2004–2012: Early career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Stephen_Amell&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: 2004–2012: Early career")]

Amell appeared in two episodes of the [fourth season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queer_as_Folk_(season_4) "Queer as Folk (season 4)") of _[Queer as Folk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queer\_as\_Folk\_(2000\_TV\_series) "Queer as Folk (2000 TV series)")_ as the Liberty Ride spinning instructor in 2004. Amell played Adam in the first season of the television series _[Dante's Cove](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dante's\_Cove "Dante's Cove")_; he was replaced in the second season by Jon Fleming. In 2007, Amell won a [Gemini Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gemini_Awards "Gemini Awards") for his guest-starring role on _[ReGenesis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ReGenesis "ReGenesis")_.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-Free-7) The same year he was also nominated for a Gemini Award in the Best Ensemble Cast Category for _[Rent-a-Goalie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rent-a-Goalie "Rent-a-Goalie")_.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-8) He had recurring roles in the TV series _[Da Kink in My Hair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Da\_Kink\_in\_My\_Hair\_(TV\_series) "Da Kink in My Hair (TV series)")_ and _[Heartland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartland\_(Canadian\_TV\_series) "Heartland (Canadian TV series)")_. On December 3, 2010, Amell joined the cast of _[The Vampire Diaries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Vampire\_Diaries "The Vampire Diaries")_ as werewolf 'Brady' for season 2.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-9) Amell starred as the real life convicted killer [Joran van der Sloot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joran_van_der_Sloot "Joran van der Sloot") in the [Lifetime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lifetime_(TV_network) "Lifetime (TV network)") film _[Justice for Natalee Holloway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justice\_for\_Natalee\_Holloway "Justice for Natalee Holloway")_ which originally aired in May 2011.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-AV-10)

On October 2, 2011, season 3 of [HBO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HBO "HBO")'s series _[Hung](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hung\_(TV\_series) "Hung (TV series)")_ premiered with Amell starring as busboy-turned-prostitute Jason, a younger rival "ho" to [Thomas Jane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_Jane "Thomas Jane")'s Ray Drecker.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-Free-7) He also appeared as Jim in the [fourth season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/90210_(season_4) "90210 (season 4)") of _[90210](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/90210\_(TV\_series) "90210 (TV series)")_.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-TV-11) Amell announced on October 28, 2011, that he had just finished filming the Christmas episode of _[New Girl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New\_Girl "New Girl")_ with [Zooey Deschanel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zooey_Deschanel "Zooey Deschanel") and [Max Greenfield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Greenfield "Max Greenfield"). He touches on the experience of filming his first "network half-hour comedy" in an interview with _Daemon's TV_.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-TV-11) On November 9, 2011, Amell was announced for the recurring role of Scottie, a paramedic on [ABC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Broadcasting_Company "American Broadcasting Company")'s _[Private Practice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Private\_Practice\_(TV\_series) "Private Practice (TV series)")_.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-12) He also played the role of Travis McKenna in _[Blue Mountain State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blue\_Mountain\_State "Blue Mountain State")_.

### 2012–2020: _Arrow_

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Stephen_Amell&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: 2012–2020: Arrow")]

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4b/Stephen_Amell_2014.jpg/250px-Stephen_Amell_2014.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Stephen_Amell_2014.jpg)

Amell on the set of _[Arrow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrow\_(TV\_series) "Arrow (TV series)")_ in September 2014

In January 2012, Amell was cast as [Oliver Queen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oliver_Queen_(Arrowverse) "Oliver Queen (Arrowverse)") in [The CW](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_CW "The CW") series _[Arrow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrow\_(TV\_series) "Arrow (TV series)")_, based on the [DC Comics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DC_Comics "DC Comics") superhero [of the same name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_Arrow "Green Arrow").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-AV-10) This series and role led to Amell appearing as the character on other superhero series on the network as part of the growing [Arrowverse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrowverse "Arrowverse"), including _[The Flash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Flash\_(2014\_TV\_series) "The Flash (2014 TV series)")_, _[Legends of Tomorrow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legends\_of\_Tomorrow "Legends of Tomorrow")_, _[Supergirl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supergirl\_(TV\_series) "Supergirl (TV series)")_, and _[Batwoman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Batwoman\_(TV\_series) "Batwoman (TV series)")_, as well as the [CW Seed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CW_Seed "CW Seed") webseries _[Vixen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vixen\_(web\_series) "Vixen (web series)")_.

Amell co-starred in _[Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Out of the Shadows](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teenage\_Mutant\_Ninja\_Turtles:\_Out\_of\_the\_Shadows\_(film) "Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Out of the Shadows (film)")_ (released on June 3, 2016) as vigilante "[Casey Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Casey_Jones_(Teenage_Mutant_Ninja_Turtles) "Casey Jones (Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles)")".[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-13) Amell announced in May 2017 that he would be participating on a special celebrity edition of _[American Ninja Warrior](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American\_Ninja\_Warrior "American Ninja Warrior")_.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-14) Amell demonstrated great physical abilities which was reflective of his athleticism in his portrayal of Oliver Queen.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-15) In 2017, he took part in the directorial debut of former _[Heartland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartland\_(Canadian\_TV\_series) "Heartland (Canadian TV series)")_ co-star [Michelle Morgan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michelle_Morgan_(actress) "Michelle Morgan (actress)"), a short film entitled _Mi Madre, My Father_, playing the estranged father of a six-year-old girl. Morgan raised funds for the production through a crowdfunding campaign.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-Morgan-16) The film premiered at the 2018 [Cannes Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cannes_Film_Festival "Cannes Film Festival").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-Cannes-17)

In March 2019, Amell announced the end of _Arrow_ with its [eighth and final season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrow_season_8 "Arrow season 8"), which premiered in October 2019 and concluded in January 2020.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-18)

### 2020–present: Post-_Arrow_

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Stephen_Amell&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: 2020–present: Post-Arrow")]

His first post-_Arrow_ project was announced in August 2019 as _[Heels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heels\_(TV\_series) "Heels (TV series)")_, a [Starz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Starz "Starz") drama series set in the world of [independent professional wrestling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Independent_professional_wrestling "Independent professional wrestling").[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-19) In December of the same year, it was announced that short-form streaming platform [Quibi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quibi "Quibi") were developing a spin-off series starring Amell and his cousin Robbie Amell, developed from their crowd-funded film _[Code 8](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Code\_8\_(2019\_film) "Code 8 (2019 film)")_.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-20) In September 2023, _Heels_ was canceled after two seasons.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-21) In February 2024, Stephen Amell was cast as Ted Black in the upcoming [NBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBC "NBC") pilot _Suits LA_, based on the [USA Network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USA_Network "USA Network") original series _[Suits](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suits\_(American\_TV\_series) "Suits (American TV series)")_.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-22) On July 19, 2024, _[Suits LA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suits\_LA "Suits LA")_ has ordered to series by NBC.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-23)

Amell plays Henry Roland, a police officer, in the [Crave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crave_(TV_network) "Crave (TV network)") crime drama series _[The Borderline](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Borderline\_(Canadian\_TV\_series) "The Borderline (Canadian TV series)")_.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-24) it debuted in February 2026.

He garnered positive reviews for his leading role in the Canadian crime film _[Little Lorraine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Little\_Lorraine "Little Lorraine")_, released in 2026.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-25)

## Professional wrestling career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Stephen_Amell&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Professional wrestling career")]

### WWE (2015)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Stephen_Amell&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: WWE (2015)")]

As an avid [professional wrestling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Professional_wrestling "Professional wrestling") fan,[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-HollywoodLifeWWE-26) Amell campaigned for a guest appearance on [WWE](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WWE "WWE")'s weekly _[Raw](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WWE\_Raw "WWE Raw")_ program.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-27)

In May 2015, it was reported that he was set to wrestle [Stardust (Cody Rhodes)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cody_Rhodes "Cody Rhodes") at WWE's [SummerSlam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SummerSlam_(2015) "SummerSlam (2015)") pay-per-view in August.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-HollywoodLifeWWE-26) Amell made his first WWE appearance on the May 25 episode of _Raw_, where he had a confrontation with Stardust.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-28) Amell returned to _Raw_ in early August; after being assaulted in the audience by Stardust, Amell got into the [ring](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wrestling_ring "Wrestling ring") to attack him until being contained by security. Following a [backstage segment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glossary_of_professional_wrestling_terms#Segment "Glossary of professional wrestling terms") with [Triple H](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Triple_H "Triple H"), it was announced that [Neville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neville_(wrestler) "Neville (wrestler)") would team with Amell to face Stardust and [King Barrett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wade_Barrett "Wade Barrett") at SummerSlam.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-29)

At the event on August 23, 2015, Amell and Neville defeated Barrett and Stardust in a [tag team match](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Professional_wrestling_tag_team_match_types "Professional wrestling tag team match types"). Amell participated in the wrestling, and, behind the scenes, wrestlers were said to have been impressed with Amell's performance.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-30)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-31) Amell became friends with Rhodes, with whom he later also worked on _Arrow_.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-BulletClub-32)

On December 21, 2015, Amell was awarded a [Slammy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slammy "Slammy") for the "Celebrity Moment of the Year" for his dive onto Stardust during the match.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-33)

### Ring of Honor (2017)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Stephen_Amell&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Ring of Honor (2017)")]

Amell returned to professional wrestling for [Ring of Honor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ring_of_Honor "Ring of Honor") on November 17, 2017, at [Survival of the Fittest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Survival_of_the_Fittest_(2017) "Survival of the Fittest (2017)").[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-34) On the day of the show, Amell joined the [Bullet Club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bullet_Club "Bullet Club")[faction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glossary_of_professional_wrestling_terms#Stable "Glossary of professional wrestling terms"), and teamed with Cody Rhodes, [Kenny Omega](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Omega "Kenny Omega"), and [The Young Bucks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Young_Bucks "The Young Bucks") (Matt and Nick Jackson) in a five-on-four tag team match. They defeated [The Addiction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Addiction_(professional_wrestling) "The Addiction (professional wrestling)") ([Christopher Daniels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Daniels "Christopher Daniels") and [Frankie Kazarian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frankie_Kazarian "Frankie Kazarian")), [Flip Gordon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flip_Gordon "Flip Gordon"), and [Scorpio Sky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scorpio_Sky "Scorpio Sky"), and Amell again participated in the wrestling, including being put through a table by The Addiction.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-35)

## Philanthropy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Stephen_Amell&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Philanthropy")]

Amell has hosted a number of successful fundraising campaigns via the crowd funded merchandise platform [Represent.com](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Represent.com "Represent.com").[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-38) In 2014, Amell partnered with the charity Fuck Cancer to raise almost a million dollars with the release of a T-shirt featuring his face on the front (with a Post-it note on his forehead and featuring the organization's name). He ended up selling over 60,000 shirts from this campaign.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-39) In January 2015, Amell launched his second Represent.com campaign featuring a word he made up, _Sinceriously_, to benefit two mental health charities: Paws and Stripes and Stand For The Silent.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] In August 2015, Amell used his guest appearance on _[WWE Raw](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WWE\_Raw "WWE Raw")_ with [Stardust](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cody_Rhodes "Cody Rhodes") to raise funds via his third campaign for children's hospice Emily's House in Toronto. The campaign raised $300,000, and Amell and Stardust presented a cheque together at Emily's House.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-40) During the Red Nose Day special of _[American Ninja Warrior](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American\_Ninja\_Warrior "American Ninja Warrior")_, Amell donated $35,000 for completing all six obstacles, and an extra obstacle, the Salmon Ladder.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-41)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Stephen_Amell&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Amell married his first wife, fellow Canadian Carolyn Lawrence, on December 8, 2007, in Toronto.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-42) The couple divorced in 2010.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-43) Amell married actress and model [Cassandra Jean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cassandra_Jean "Cassandra Jean") on December 25, 2012, in a private ceremony in [the Caribbean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Caribbean "The Caribbean"),[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-44) and for a second time in [New Orleans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Orleans "New Orleans") on May 26, 2013.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-45) The couple have a daughter who was born on October 15, 2013. They have a son, born May 13, 2022.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-46) Amell revealed on his Instagram that he became a dual citizen of Canada and the United States and took his U.S. citizenship oath in August 2022 at Dodger Stadium.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-47)

## Controversies

Amell's statements and behavior have occasionally drawn controversy. In September 2015, after a [Muslim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muslims "Muslims") student was arrested for [bringing a disassembled digital clock to his high school](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmed_Mohamed_clock_incident "Ahmed Mohamed clock incident") in [Irving](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irving,_Texas "Irving, Texas"), Texas, Amell tweeted, "Stereotyping Texas isn't any better than stereotyping Ahmed".[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-48) The post drew criticism online, prompting Amell to take a break from social media.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-49)[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-50)[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-51)

In 2018, Amell tweeted "my âpölògīés"[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-52) in response to criticism about his failure to use the [acute accent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acute_accent "Acute accent") while tweeting singer [Beyoncé](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beyonc%C3%A9 "Beyoncé")'s name.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-53)[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-54) After he was accused by online commenters of disrespecting [black names](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African-American_names "African-American names"), he said he had omitted the accent while being "lazy in the midst of a mediocre joke".[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-55)

In 2020, during the [Black Lives Matter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Lives_Matter "Black Lives Matter")[protests](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Floyd_protests "George Floyd protests"), Amell was criticized by comic book writer [Tee Franklin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tee_Franklin "Tee Franklin") and others for saying that racism is a systemic problem but that he had not personally "seen it in action".[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-56)

In 2021, Amell was asked to leave a [Delta Air Lines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delta_Air_Lines "Delta Air Lines") flight traveling from Austin to Los Angeles for yelling at his wife.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-57) He later said he was intoxicated at the time.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-58)[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-59)

In July 2023, Amell was criticized for comments he made at a fan convention regarding the [2023 SAG-AFTRA strike](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_SAG-AFTRA_strike "2023 SAG-AFTRA strike"). While he expressed support for [SAG-AFTRA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SAG-AFTRA "SAG-AFTRA") as his union, he called striking a "reductive negotiating tactic" and "myopic" and seemed to criticize that the strike banned him from promoting the second season of _Heels_.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-60)[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-61) He later clarified his opinion, saying that while he does not like striking, he "[understands] fundamentally why we're here" and stated that his support for the union was unconditional and that he stood with them.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-62) Amell did not attend the _Arrow_ cast reunion on the picket line outside the Warner Bros. studio lot in [Burbank, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burbank,_California "Burbank, California"), as he was in New York City at the time, but on the day of the reunion, he was photographed on the picket line in front of the [Warner Bros. Discovery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warner_Bros._Discovery "Warner Bros. Discovery") offices in New York and reportedly sent his regards to his former showrunners in California. [Marc Guggenheim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marc_Guggenheim "Marc Guggenheim"), executive producer of _Arrow_ and organizer of the revival, interpreted his attendance in New York as a symbolic stand in solidarity.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-63)[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-64)
